title: Connection lifespan negotiation and fragment semantic mapping for SSE streaming and toolcall interoperability
creator: Nora Cheng
description: Problem: Customers observe either duplicate function/tool invocations or truncated structured outputs after intermittent network blips. Root cause is ambiguous fragment semantics and lack of an explicit connection-lifespan handshake between client and server. Goal: introduce a minimal, backward-compatible negotiation layer that lets clients and Redwood runtime agree on fragment lifetime, merge semantics, and toolcall boundary mapping so reconnects can safely rehydrate incomplete streams without producing duplicate tool invocations or corrupt structured outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Clients that advertise the new handshake bit receive a resume token and a TTL for fragments; reconnect within TTL should reattach and continue without duplicate tool/function calls
If client does not advertise capability, server falls back to current best-effort resume (no change for legacy clients)
Structured-object boundaries (JSON/ToolCall blocks) are annotated with a fragment-semantics header so the resume logic can perform deterministic merges
End-to-end regression tests demonstrate <0.1% increase in tail-latency and a reduction in duplicate-toolcall incidents to zero in simulated reconnect scenarios
spec_changes: Add optional 'X-RW-Stream-Capabilities' header to initial SSE handshake: comma-separated capabilities (resume-v2, fragment-ttl, semantic-tags)
Handshake response: 'RW-Resume-Token' and 'RW-Fragment-TTL' headers included when resume-v2 supported; TTL in seconds
Embed per-chunk metadata line with 'fragment-id', 'sequence', 'semantic-tag' (e.g., 'toolcall-start', 'toolcall-mid', 'toolcall-end', 'json-root') as a lightweight JSONL prefix for each chunk

Deterministic merge algorithm: on reconnect, server supplies the resume cursor and the semantic-tag sequence. Client may re-send last N fragments; server uses fragment-id+sequence and semantic-tag to de-duplicate and stitch toolcall boundaries atomically
Backoff/expiry: fragments older than TTL are treated as lost; server emits explicit 'fragment-gap' event detailing failed boundaries to help client fail-fast or fallback to re-request full response
Telemetry hooks: emit metrics 'stream.resume.attempt', 'stream.resume.success', 'stream.duplicate-toolcall.detected', and histograms for 'resume.latency' and 'merge.duration'
Compatibility: legacy clients receive no new headers; feature flags gate server-side resume-v2 rollout
test_plan: Unit: parser tests for chunk metadata extraction and semantic-tag state machine
Integration: local reconnect harness that simulates network drop during toolcall boundary; assert no duplicate tool invocation in runtime logs
Chaos: run in staging with packet-loss injected (0.5%-5%) across 24h; compare duplicate-toolcall incidents to baseline
Compatibility: smoke tests against older SDKs to ensure no change in legacy behavior
Performance: benchmark tail-latency at p95/p99 for streaming paths with and without resume-v2 enabled
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 2% of hosted traffic and all Dedicated test clusters for 48h; collect telemetry and error budgets
Gradual ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks pending metrics
Fallback: automatic disable if 'stream.duplicate-toolcall.detected' rate > 0.01% over rolling 1h
Client SDKs: release companion patch with handshake and resume logic; document handshake header and chunk prefix format in Dev Portal
comments: 2026-02-27 Nora Cheng: Created ticket after on-call reported two incidents where users saw duplicate reruns of external tool calls following mobile network flaps. Logged initial incident links in Confluence.

2026-03-01 Miguel Alvarez: Drafted handshake sketch — proposing 'X-RW-Stream-Capabilities' and 'RW-Resume-Token' headers. Added example SSE payload with metadata prefix. Pushed initial branch: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/tree/feat/resume-v2
2026-03-04 Design review (Priya Rao): Approved semantic-tag taxonomy (toolcall-start/mid/end, json-root, stdout-fragment). Requested examples for mixed text+functioncall outputs.

2026-03-06 Platform review (Evan McCoy): Raised concern about resume token size when KV cache is evicted; suggested server-side short-lived token mapping (token -> persisted fragment list) rather than embedding full state in token
2026-03-08 Miguel Alvarez: Implemented prototype token mapping (server-side index) and added 'RW-Fragment-TTL' header. Benchmarked merge duration: median 1.8ms, p99 9.4ms on c6g.xlarge nodes

2026-03-10 QA (Lina Park): Integration tests added to CI. Found edge case when a client reconnects and re-sends overlapping fragments with different sequence numbers — fixed de-dupe rule to prefer server-seen fragment-id and drop client duplicates
2026-03-12 Nora Cheng: Merged spec into design doc. Preparing canary run; coordinating SDK patch release notes and adding observability dashboards for resume metrics
